content.comment_body: Hello. I had good experiences with [product_name] V8.0, but recent changes with FS04 units require me to upgrade to V8.1. The update went smoothly on my Windows PC as expected, but I keep hitting an error on my MacBook using OS X Sierra when I unpack with Stuffit and try running the setup.app (it reports a damaged file, similar to other posts). Adjusting the security and permissions didn't help since now the only install option is 'app store and identified developers.' Trying the online update method from [product_name] itself fails with a 'File Required for the update cannot be found on the computer' error. Any suggestions?
Check out this discussion, particularly the comment from [user_name]. The error 'java.lang.UnsupportedOperationExeption: adapter type is not support' may point to the same issue you’re experiencing.

Let me clarify my situation: [product_name] V8.0 won't upgrade to V8.1 on my MacBook and seems to be searching for a missing file in a specific directory. Possibly I installed the software in a non-default location. Does anyone know which file is required and where it's located?
Could you share a screenshot of the error message?

Here’s a screenshot showing the error that appears when I click update. I’ve also tried manually downloading and using Stuffit Expander, but it still won’t work. I’m sharing the Java environment path for [product_name]; maybe someone can identify an installation error. I’ve attempted both installing and reinstalling.
Here’s the first half of my system screen.

Here’s the rest of the Java Path. If nothing works, I may have to buy a new CD with V8.1. It only recently became available here with my local distributor in South Africa. If troubleshooting takes too long, I suggest we move on. What concerns me more is the app crashing on my iPad (mentioned elsewhere).

A response came from [company_name] Support: Thank you for your inquiry. As shown at [url], [product_name] requires Mac OS X 10.6 Snow Leopard, Mac OS X Lion, Mac OS X Mountain Lion, or Mac OS X Mavericks. MacOS Sierra is not supported for [product_name]. Best regards, Industry Automation and Drive Technologies Technical Support. Well, that settles it. Using my MacBook is no longer possible.

Hi. You need to expand the downloaded update file with Stuffit, but not every Stuffit version is compatible. Avoid using Safari as it automatically tries to expand the file during download. Installation should work on Sierra 10.12.6—though I haven’t personally tried transferring projects to my [product_name].

Hello [user_name], thank you! Your advice succeeded where [company_name] support fell short. I downloaded the update via a Windows device, then used Stuffit on the Mac for extraction, and it worked immediately. The software now works perfectly for uploading/downloading projects and monitoring. For other Mac users: try downloading the update using Firefox or Chrome, though Firefox didn’t work for me. Another tip—Mac saves the app file under users\[user_name]\applications, not in the main 'Applications' folder. You might open the old version by accident; after upgrading, I deleted the outdated version. Thanks again, [user_name]!

OSX automatically unpacks downloaded files, which you can verify by comparing the file size from the download site and your local upgrade copy (e.g., 113.1 MB vs. 114.3 MB). To prevent auto-unpacking, adjust your Safari settings and try downloading the free app Unarchiver from the App Store. If you download and manually unpack the file, installation should proceed normally. Note that in Sierra, the 'Allow from all Sources' option in Security is removed. You can restore it in Gatekeeper by running: 'sudo spctl --master-disable'. Sierra isn’t officially listed as supported, but once configured, it works fine.
A new question posted by [user_name] was moved to a separate thread titled 'Can't open [product_name] and Program has no reaction.' Best regards, [user_name]_Moderator

analysis.insight_summary: Users face repeated compatibility and installation challenges when upgrading [product_name] from V8.0 to V8.1 on MacOS Sierra. Common errors include file corruption and missing required files. While the upgrade works without issue on Windows, official [company_name] support confirms MacOS Sierra is not supported for [product_name], leaving users who rely on recent Macs frustrated and limited in their options.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to install and upgrade smoothly on newer MacOS versions and to receive helpful error messages or troubleshooting support when problems arise.
